title: Théorie arithmétique. Théorie de Galois des motifs (1965) : notes manuscites (s.d.), tapuscrit (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: Grothendieck's 1965 notes on the Galois theory of motives, in which a Tannakian group G(X,xi) is attached to a variety X (or motive) and a fibre functor xi. The page is in three parts.

(1) Top lines. These finish a sentence from an earlier manuscript page; the previous page in the folder is an unrelated Bourbaki typescript. The statement reads: '(results from the conjunction of the Hodge and Tate conjectures (over a finite field), at least if X varies). Characterisation of the image??'
In modern terms the most plausible reading is as follows.
- Some comparison statement is being deduced. The candidate is that the image of the Galois group (or of the Mumford-Tate group) in the motivic group is as large as possible: it equals, or is open in, the motivic Galois group G(X).
- This would follow from Hodge plus Tate. The Hodge conjecture identifies the motivic group with the Mumford-Tate group. The Tate conjecture, including over finite fields, identifies it with the Zariski closure of the l-adic Galois image, using specialisation when X moves in a family.
- 'Caractérisation de l'image ??' then asks for the actual l-adic image, not just its Zariski closure. This is essentially the Mumford-Tate / open-image problem.
- He then proposes to look at X defined over a subfield k of C, of finite type or algebraically closed, e.g. k = Q-bar. Here only the Hodge side remains and motives over Q-bar are compared with those over C.

(2) 'Analyser l'exemple en termes de pi_1 ...'. He wants to analyse the example via the (Tannakian or étale) fundamental group.

(3) Bracketed paragraph, case of base field R; the margin diagram shows X over R with its base change to C.
- A real variety X gives, via its complex points with complex conjugation, a fibre functor xi_inf. It also gives an involution, i.e. an element of order 2 ('fibration d'ordre 2', possibly 'involution').
- Complex conjugation conjugates G(X,xi) into the group attached to the conjugate fibre functor; the transcription has G(X.xi) 'conjuguée' to G(X,xi).
- He claims that the functor sending a motive M over R to (xi(M), its Hodge structure, the real structure / involution defined by the fibration at infinity) is fully faithful.
- In modern language: the Betti-Hodge realisation of motives over R, with the action of F_inf (complex conjugation on X(C), combined with conjugation of Hodge types), is fully faithful. This would follow from the Hodge conjecture over C by Gal(C/R)-descent of Hom-spaces.
- The infinite place is thus treated as an analogue of a finite place: F_inf plays the role of Frobenius, as an order-2 element of the motivic Galois group.

(4) 'Pb': study how the Hodge structure of a variable complex variety varies, as a function of the initial datum at the infinite place. This is the variation of Hodge structure / period-map problem, posed in the motivic-Galois setting.
errors: The full-faithfulness claim for motives over R is conditional on the Hodge conjecture; as written it is stated without the hypothesis, though the context shows conjectural statements throughout.
Readings of 'T_inf(Z)', 'fibration d'ordre 2', 'k t.f. clos' are uncertain; the precise meaning of xi_inf in T_inf(Z) cannot be fixed from the image.

ideas.what: Hodge plus Tate conjectures together imply that the motivic group coincides with the Mumford-Tate group and with the Zariski closure of the l-adic image; the question of characterising the image itself
ideas.modern_name: Mumford-Tate conjecture / open image problem for motivic Galois groups
ideas.where_published: Not in EGA/SGA; motives mentioned in Grothendieck-Serre correspondence and 'Standard conjectures' (1969), neither treats this

ideas.what: Motives over R realised as Hodge structures plus an involution (complex conjugation / F_inf), with this realisation conjectured fully faithful
ideas.modern_name: Real Hodge structures with F_inf; Hodge realisation of motives over R (Deligne's F_inf)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Deligne, 'Valeurs de fonctions L et périodes d'intégrales' (1979); Deligne-Milne-Ogus-Shih (1982)

ideas.what: Complex conjugation acting on fibre functors and conjugating the motivic Galois group; the infinite place giving an element of order 2, analogous to Frobenius
ideas.modern_name: Frobenius at infinity in the motivic Galois group (cf. the element c in the Taniyama group)

ideas.what: Study how Hodge structures vary in families, in terms of the motivic/Galois data
ideas.modern_name: Variation of Hodge structure, period maps, Mumford-Tate groups in families (generic vs special points)

missed.claim: As early as 1965 Grothendieck formulates that the realisation of real motives into Hodge structures plus real structure / involution (F_inf) should be fully faithful. He also treats complex conjugation as an order-2 element acting on the motivic Galois group. Both are usually attributed to Deligne's late-1970s formalism.
missed.quote: Le foncteur M ~> (xi(M)_xi, + structure de Hodge, + réalification défini par fibration) est pleinement fidèle.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is a historical priority point: the F_inf / real-place analogue of Frobenius in the Tannakian motivic setting appears in Grothendieck's 1965 notes. It is a direct consequence of the Hodge conjecture, so it is not mathematically new.

missed.claim: Grothendieck asks for a characterisation of the actual image, beyond its Zariski closure, of the Galois representation in the motivic group. He also asks for an analysis of how Hodge structures vary with the datum at the infinite place.
missed.quote: Caractérisation de l'image ?? ... Pb étudier comment varie la structure de Hodge pour une vt complexe variable, en fonction de la donnée de départ sur la vt inf
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Both problems were developed independently later (Serre on open images; Deligne/André on Mumford-Tate groups in families). This page only shows that Grothendieck posed them early, without content beyond the questions.

deep.surprise_reason: The ideas are early anticipations (1965) of the Frobenius-at-infinity / real-Hodge-structure formalism and of Mumford-Tate-type questions, which are later credited to Deligne and Serre. They are sketchy and conditional, and are standard consequences of the Hodge and Tate conjectures. The interest is mainly historical priority.
transcription_corrections: 'k t.f.[?] clos' probably reads 'k alg. clos' or 'k de type fini' — uncertain.
'au moins si X variable' probably reads 'au moins si X varie' (in a family).
Margin diagram: X over R with arrows to C and R (base change X_C).
